   108	## Banned AI/Software Language (enforced in both blueprint AND Lean code)
   109	The blueprint reads as a **mathematical document**, not software documentation. The following patterns are banned in ALL reader-facing text (section titles, theorem names, proof sketches, remarks, chapter preambles) and in ALL Lean docstrings, comments, and section names:
   110	
   111	### Banned terms → replacements:
   112	| Banned | Use instead |
   113	|--------|------------|
   114	| "Assembly" (as section/chapter title) | "Proof of [theorem]", "Construction", "Composition" |
   115	| "Pipeline" | "reduction", "construction", "proof chain" |
   116	| "Bridge" (as noun for a connection) | "connection", name by mathematical content |
   117	| "Handoff" / "hand off" | "transition", "continuation", or drop entirely |
   118	| "In this blueprint" / "Within this blueprint" | "here", "in what follows", or omit |
   119	| "Honest" (as adjective for rigorous) | "exact", "faithful", "unconditional", "complete" |
   120	| "Glue layer" | "intermediate construction", "connecting results" |
   121	| "Re-export" / "reexport" | "provides", "re-states" |
   122	| "Wiring" / "wire up" | "connecting", "composing", "combining" |
   123	| "Package" (as noun for a data bundle) | "form", "data", "structure" |
   124	| "Sorry-free" | acceptable only in Lean-specific technical context |
   125	
   126	### Additional rules:
   127	- **Section names in Lean**: use mathematical terms (`section QuantumSoundness`, `section SelfImprovement`, `section PastingLemma`), not organizational terms (`section Assembly`, `section Pipeline`).
   128	- **Internal LaTeX labels** (e.g., `\label{ch:soundness}`) are not reader-facing and need not be renamed if doing so would break cross-references. But NEW labels should follow the standard.
   129	- **Definitions that are actually theorems**: if a statement asserts a mathematical fact, it must be `\begin{theorem}`, not `\begin{definition}`. Definitions introduce new objects; theorems prove properties.
   130	
   131	## `\uses` Dependency Guidelines
   132	- **Statement `\uses`**: list only what's needed to *state* the result (typically definitions of the objects involved). Keep minimal — transitive deps are automatic.
   133	- **Proof `\uses`**: list only what the proof *actually calls*. Don't list definitions unless the proof unfolds that definition.
   134	- **Never self-reference**: a proof's `\uses` must NOT include the label of the theorem it proves.
   135	
   136	## Recording Formalization-Only Lemmas
   137	Some Lean lemmas are genuine proof infrastructure rather than named statements
   138	from the original papers. These must be traceable without making the blueprint
   139	look as if the paper stated them.
   140	
   141	- If a declaration directly formalizes a paper or blueprint statement, record
   142	  it as usual with `\lean{...}` on that statement and cite the relevant source.
   143	- If a public declaration is an auxiliary lemma introduced only for the Lean
   144	  proof, make that status explicit. Its Lean docstring should say that it is a
   145	  formalization-only auxiliary lemma and should name the nearby paper equation,
   146	  line range, or blueprint result it supports.
   147	- If such an auxiliary declaration is important enough to be referenced from
   148	  the blueprint, give it a clearly subordinate blueprint node, for example
   149	  `[Formalization support for ...]`, and state in the first sentence that the
   150	  lemma is not a named statement of the paper but isolates a step used in the
   151	  Lean proof.
   152	- Connect auxiliary nodes to the corresponding result from the paper with `\uses{...}` from
   153	  the proof that actually calls them. Do not add them only to silence a sync
   154	  warning; the dependency edge should explain where the auxiliary result is
   155	  used.
   156	- Do not mark an auxiliary node with proof-level `\leanok` unless its Lean proof
   157	  is complete and `#print axioms` has no `sorryAx`. Statement-level `\leanok`
   158	  is acceptable only when the Lean statement is intentionally recorded but the
   159	  proof remains tracked as incomplete.

   162	- `content.tex` is a router: `\input{chapter/ch01_intro}` etc.
   163	- Each chapter is a separate file in `chapter/`
   164	- Definitions/theorems numbered within chapters: `\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[chapter]`

   166	## Lean Blueprint Macros
   167	- `\lean{Namespace.DeclName}` — links to Lean declaration
   168	- `\leanok` — context-sensitive marker; see "Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`" below
   169	- `\uses{label1, label2}` — declares dependency edges for the graph
   170	- `\notready` — marks as not ready for formalization (orange in graph)
   171	- `\mathlibok` — already in Mathlib (dark green in graph; see legend note below)
   172	
   173	### Statement-level vs proof-level `\leanok`
   174	
   175	`\leanok` is context-sensitive for human review and graph interpretation. The same macro is used for two different claims, so reviewers should read it by placement rather than by raw token count.
   176	
   177	**Statement-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside a `theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, or `definition` environment, on its own line immediately after `\lean{...}`. It says that the corresponding Lean declaration exists and that its statement matches the blueprint or paper statement. It does **not** say that the Lean proof already exists or is complete. For definitions, this is the only `\leanok` marker.
   178	
   179	**Proof-level `\leanok`.** Place this inside the matching `proof` environment, preferably as the first line after `\begin{proof}`. The canonical current placement is the theorem `thm:commutativity-points` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`, where the statement block has `\leanok` immediately after `\lean{...}` and the proof block begins with another `\leanok`. This marker says that the Lean proof is complete and free of unresolved `sorry` or unjustified project-level `axiom` shortcuts. In particular, `#print axioms <decl>` must show no `sorryAx`, and the declaration must satisfy the broader blocker rules in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and [`docs/project_conventions.md`](project_conventions.md).
   180	
   181	A theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary node is **fully formalized in Lean if and only if it has both markers**: statement-level `\leanok` in the statement block and proof-level `\leanok` in the proof block. Statement-level without proof-level means “the statement has been transcribed and matched, but the proof is not yet certified complete.” Definitions have no proof block, so statement-level `\leanok` alone is enough there.
   182	
   183	Excerpt from `blueprint/src/chapter/ch08_commutativity.tex:8-19`:
   184	
   185	```latex
   186	\begin{theorem}[Commutativity of the point measurements]\label{thm:commutativity-points}
   187	  \lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.CommutativityPoints.commutativityPoints}
   188	  \leanok
   189	  \uses{def:good-strategy, def:approx_delta}
   190	  Let $(\psi,A,B,L)$ be an $(\eps,\delta,\gamma)$-good symmetric strategy.
   191	\end{theorem}
   192	\begin{proof}
   193	  \leanok
   194	  The strategy passes the diagonal lines test with probability $1-\gamma$.
   195	\end{proof}
   196	```
   197	
   198	**Current CI behavior.** The advisory Blueprint ↔ Lean sync check in [`docs/ci-blueprint-sync.md`](ci-blueprint-sync.md) distinguishes the two placements. Only proof-level `\leanok` whose axiom closure contains `sorryAx` (or whose harness output cannot be parsed) is reported as an **error**. Statement-level-only `\leanok` with the same finding is downgraded to a **warning**, because statement-level does not claim proof completeness. Each audit line is annotated with the observed placement so reviewers can tell statement-sync work apart from proof-completion work.
   199	
   200	`leanblueprint` does not use distinct macro names for these two claims, so audits must distinguish them by environment context rather than by raw `\leanok` counts. A future split such as `\leanokstmt` / `\leanokproof` could make that distinction explicit, but that is only a possible later cleanup; the current convention is to keep `\leanok` and rely on placement.
   201	
   202	A recurring historical example is the chapter 4 `Q/X/\widehat X/P` witness
   203	layer.  Once Lean has construction theorems deriving the displayed identities
   204	and estimates from the rank-reduction, sigma-range, positive-Gram, native
   205	spectral-theorem, or rectangular-SVD hypotheses, the corresponding blueprint
   206	entries may carry `\leanok`.  A declaration that merely projects an identity
   207	from an opaque data record is not enough by itself, and a theorem depending on
   208	extra rectangular-SVD data should not be used as evidence for an unconditional
   209	paper statement unless a separate construction supplies that data.

   219	1. Edit `blueprint/src/references.bib` (standalone, AuthorYYYYKeyword keys)
   220	2. Run `texra-blueprint bbl` from the repository root — it regenerates
   221	   `blueprint/src/web.bbl` from the `\cite` keys in the blueprint sources.
   222	   `web.bbl` is not committed (`.gitignore` covers `*.bbl`); every CI job
   223	   that runs the web build regenerates it first, and so must a local run.

   230	   entry in `blueprint/src/references.bib` with `type = {Paper-gap note}`,

    21	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}

    32	/-- A uniform consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of

    35	    {X Y Outcome iota : Type*}
    36	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Nonempty X]
    37	    [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y] [Nonempty Y]
    38	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    39	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    40	    (e : X ≃ Y) (A B : Y → Outcome → Op iota)
    41	    (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    42	    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution X)
    43	        (fun x a => A (e x) a) (fun x a => B (e x) a) psi =
    44	      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Y) A B psi := by
    45	  unfold consistencyDefect
    46	  simpa using avgOver_uniform_equiv e (fun x =>
    47	    ∑ a : Outcome, ∑ b : Outcome,
    48	      if a = b then 0 else
    49	        (inner ℂ psi ((EuclideanSpace.equiv iota ℂ).symm
    50	          (((A (e x) a) * (B (e x) b)).mulVec psi))).re)

    52	/-- A consistency defect is invariant under a bijective relabeling of both
    53	outcome families. -/

    55	    {X Alpha Beta iota : Type*}
    56	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
    57	    [Fintype Alpha] [DecidableEq Alpha]
    58	    [Fintype Beta] [DecidableEq Beta]
    59	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    60	    (mu : Distribution X) (e : Beta ≃ Alpha)
    61	    (A B : X → Alpha → Op iota) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
    62	    consistencyDefect mu
    63	        (fun x b => A x (e b)) (fun x b => B x (e b)) psi =
    64	      consistencyDefect mu A B psi := by
    65	  unfold consistencyDefect
    66	  apply avgOver_congr
    67	  intro x
    68	  let term : Alpha → Alpha → ℝ := fun a b =>
    69	    if a = b then 0 else

    72	  calc
    73	    _ = ∑ a : Beta, ∑ b : Beta, term (e a) (e b) := by
    74	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    75	      intro a _
    76	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    77	      intro b _

    79	      by_cases hab : a = b
    80	      · subst b

    82	      · have heab : e a ≠ e b := fun h => hab (e.injective h)

     8	/-!
     9	# The directly indexed low-degree game
    10	
    11	The low-degree game used by the Pauli-basis combining argument is needed in
    12	dimension `2 * m + 2`.  The existing conditionally linear game represents a
    13	coordinate index by an equally sized fiber in the scalar field and therefore
    14	requires the dimension to divide the field size.  This file gives the separate
    15	directly indexed variant which samples that index directly.
    16	
    17	The geometric line carrier records the sampled coordinate, and line evaluation
    18	uses an `Option` outcome rather than assigning a value when a point does not
    19	determine one.  The game retains the point, axis-line, and diagonal-line answer
    20	formats and the nine ordered type branches of the original low-degree game.
    21	
    22	The `Transport` modules relate the direct game to the seed-indexed game and to
    23	the mature low individual degree test interface: `Transport.Correspondence`
    24	identifies coordinates, answers, and the question law of the two QPBT
    25	presentations; `Transport.SeedFiber` dilates a seed-indexed strategy to a
    26	direct strategy by a correlated residue register, and `Transport.SeedFiberValue`
    27	shows that the dilation preserves the value exactly; `Transport.Questions`
    28	reads mature lines as canonical direct questions and rebases direct answers;
    29	`Transport.Strategy` reads one coordinate of a projective direct strategy as a
    30	mature `ProjStrat`, with exact Born-weight formulas for both adapters;
    31	`Transport.Consistency` reexpresses the three single-polynomial LDT consistency
    32	relations in direct coordinates, the first two at a fixed tuple coordinate; and
    33	`Transport.BranchComparison`, `Transport.DiagonalRecursion`, and
    34	`Transport.PassConversion` convert a value bound of the direct game into the
    35	pass hypothesis of the mature low individual degree theorem for every
    36	coordinate strategy.  `GameValue` supplies the rejection calculus relating the
    37	direct value to the mature branch weights.

   147	/-- A complete measurement is determined by its effects. -/
   148	theorem ext {M N : Measurement α d} (h : ∀ a, M.effect a = N.effect a) :
   149	    M = N := by
   150	  cases M with
   151	  | mk M hM =>
   152	      cases N with
   153	      | mk N hN =>
   154	          cases M with
   155	          | mk effectM posM leM =>
   156	              cases N with
   157	              | mk effectN posN leN =>
   158	                  simp only at h
   159	                  have heffect : effectM = effectN := funext h
   160	                  subst effectN
   161	                  rfl
   162	
   163	/-- Relabeling along `f` and then along `g` is relabeling along `g ∘ f`: the
   164	fiber of `g ∘ f` over `c` is the disjoint union of the fibers of `f` over the
   165	fiber of `g` over `c`, and regrouping a finite sum of effects along it does not
   166	change the sum. -/
   167	theorem postprocess_comp {γ : Type*} [Fintype γ]
   168	    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
   169	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
   170	    (M.postprocess f).postprocess g = M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a)) := by
   171	  classical
   172	  apply ext
   173	  intro c
   174	  calc
   175	    ((M.postprocess f).postprocess g).effect c =
   176	        ∑ b : β, if g b = c then
   177	          ∑ a : α, if f a = b then M.effect a else 0
   178	        else 0 := by
   179	          change (∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b : β => g b = c),
   180	            ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a : α => f a = b), M.effect a) = _
   181	          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   182	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   183	          intro b _
   184	          by_cases hgb : g b = c
   185	          · simp only [hgb, if_true]
   186	            rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   187	          · simp [hgb]
   188	    _ = ∑ b : β, ∑ a : α,
   189	        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
   190	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   191	          intro b _
   192	          by_cases hgc : g b = c <;> simp [hgc]
   193	    _ = ∑ a : α, ∑ b : β,
   194	        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
   195	          rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   196	    _ = ∑ a : α,
   197	        if g (f a) = c then M.effect a else 0 := by
   198	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   199	          intro a _
   200	          by_cases hgc : g (f a) = c
   201	          · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (f a)]
   202	            · simp [hgc]
   203	            · intro b _ hba
   204	              by_cases hfa : f a = b
   205	              · exact (hba hfa.symm).elim
   206	              · simp [hfa]
   207	            · simp
   208	          · have hzero :
   209	                (∑ b : β,
   210	                  if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0) = 0 := by
   211	              apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   212	              intro b _
   213	              by_cases hfa : f a = b
   214	              · subst b
   215	                simp [hgc]
   216	              · simp [hfa]
   217	            simp [hgc, hzero]
   218	    _ = (M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a))).effect c := by
   219	          change _ = ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter
   220	            (fun a : α => g (f a) = c), M.effect a
   221	          rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   222	
   223	end Measurement

    28	/-! ## Equality of the two consistency formulations -/
    29	
    30	-- The following exported identities identify pure-state expectation with the
    31	-- Euclidean quadratic form used in the consistency calculations below.  They
    32	-- send a pure state to its Euclidean coordinate vector and identify the
    33	-- quadratic form of that vector with evaluation in the associated density
    34	-- state; they are stated for an arbitrary finite index type in
    35	-- `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/DistanceTheorems/Support.lean`.
    36	export MIPStarRE.QPBT.DistanceCalculus (pureStateEuclideanVector
    37	  pureStateEuclideanVector_apply pureStateEuclideanVector_norm
    38	  pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev)
    39	
    40	/-- For complete projective families and a pure bipartite state, the LDT
    41	consistency relation is exactly the QPBT off-diagonal defect.  In
    42	particular, changing between the density and vector formulations incurs no
    43	loss in the error parameter. -/
    44	theorem consRel_iff_consistencyDefect
    45	    {Question Outcome iotaA iotaB : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype Question] [DecidableEq Question]
    47	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    48	    [Fintype iotaA] [DecidableEq iotaA]
    49	    [Fintype iotaB] [DecidableEq iotaB]
    50	    [Nonempty (iotaA × iotaB)]
    51	    (psi : PureState (iotaA × iotaB))
    52	    (mu : Distribution Question) (hmu : mu.IsProbability)
    53	    (A : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaA)
    54	    (B : Question → ProjMeas Outcome iotaB) (delta : ℝ) :
    55	    ConsRel (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
    56	        (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) delta ↔
    57	      consistencyDefect mu
    58	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    59	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    60	        (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) ≤ delta := by
    61	  let AM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
    62	    fun x => DistanceCalculus.leftPlacedMeasurement
    63	      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (A x).toMeasurement)
    64	  let BM : Question → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (iotaA × iotaB) :=
    65	    fun x => DistanceCalculus.rightPlacedMeasurement
    66	      (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement)
    67	  have hAM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
    68	      (AM x).effect a = heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1 := rfl
    69	  have hBM (x : Question) (a : Outcome) :
    70	      (BM x).effect a = heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a) := rfl
    71	  have hdefect :
    72	      consistencyDefect mu
    73	          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    74	          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    75	          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
    76	        bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
    77	          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
    78	    calc
    79	      consistencyDefect mu
    80	          (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).outcome a) 1)
    81	          (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).outcome a))
    82	          (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) =
    83	          1 - avgOver mu (fun x => ∑ a,
    84	            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
    85	              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
    86	            simpa only [hAM, hBM] using
    87	              DistanceCalculus.consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap
    88	                mu AM BM (pureStateEuclideanVector psi) hmu
    89	                  (pureStateEuclideanVector_norm psi)
    90	      _ = avgOver mu (fun x => 1 - ∑ a,
    91	            DistanceCalculus.stateQForm (pureStateEuclideanVector psi)
    92	              ((AM x).effect a * (BM x).effect a)) := by
    93	            rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_of_isProbability mu hmu]
    94	      _ = bipartiteConsError (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB)) mu
    95	          (fun x => (A x).toSubMeas) (fun x => (B x).toSubMeas) := by
    96	            unfold bipartiteConsError
    97	            apply avgOver_congr
    98	            intro x
    99	            rw [qBipartiteConsDefect_of_measurements
   100	              (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB))
   101	              (A x).toMeasurement (B x).toMeasurement]
   102	            rw [ev_one_of_isNormalized (psi : QuantumState (iotaA × iotaB))
   103	              psi.toQuantumState_isNormalized]
   104	            congr 1
   105	            apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   106	            intro a _
   107	            rw [hAM, hBM]
   108	            rw [DistanceCalculus.placed_product_stateQForm_eq]
   109	            exact pureState_stateQForm_eq_ev psi
   110	              (opTensor ((A x).outcome a) ((B x).outcome a))
   111	  constructor
   112	  · intro h
   113	    rw [hdefect]
   114	    exact h.offDiagonalBound
   115	  · intro h
   116	    refine ⟨?_⟩
   117	    rw [← hdefect]
   118	    exact h

     4	# Low-degree consistency transport
     5	
     6	This module identifies the low individual degree polynomial outcomes with the
     7	bounded polynomial representatives used by the directly indexed QPBT game.  It
     8	also transports complete measurements and their evaluation postprocessings
     9	without changing either coordinate order or consistency error.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	- `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:393-458`
    14	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex:180-202`
    15	- `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`
    16	-/

    30	private theorem directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le
    31	    (D : DirectLdParams) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin D.m) (DirectScalarQ D))
    32	    (hp : ∀ i, MvPolynomial.degreeOf i p ≤ D.d) (i : Fin D.m) :
    33	    MvPolynomial.degreeOf i (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev p) ≤ D.d := by
    34	  rw [← Fin.rev_rev i,
    35	    MvPolynomial.degreeOf_rename_of_injective Fin.rev_injective]
    36	  exact hp (Fin.rev i)
    37	
    38	private theorem ldtPolynomial_ext
    39	    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    40	    {g h : MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial params} (hpoly : g.poly = h.poly) : g = h := by
    41	  cases g with
    42	  | mk gp hg =>
    43	      cases h with
    44	      | mk hp hh =>
    45	          simp only at hpoly
    46	          subst hp
    47	          rfl
    48	
    49	/-- Bounded QPBT polynomial representatives are equivalent to LDT
    50	polynomial outcomes.  The variable renaming is the same coordinate reversal
    51	as `directPointEquiv`, so evaluation retains the direct coordinate order. -/
    52	noncomputable def directPolyEquivPolynomial (D : DirectLdParams) :
    53	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    54	    PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d ≃
    55	      MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters := by
    56	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    57	  refine
    58	    { toFun := fun g =>
    59	        { poly := MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1
    60	          lowIndividualDegree := directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le D g.1
    61	            (degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc g.2) }
    62	      invFun := fun g =>
    63	        ⟨MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.poly, ?_⟩
    64	      left_inv := ?_
    65	      right_inv := ?_ }
    66	  · rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree]
    67	    intro s hs i
    68	    exact (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mp
    69	      (directPolynomialRename_degreeOf_le D g.poly g.lowIndividualDegree i)) s hs
    70	  · intro g
    71	    apply Subtype.ext
    72	    change MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev
    73	      (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1) = g.1
    74	    rw [MvPolynomial.rename_rename]
    75	    rw [show Fin.rev ∘ Fin.rev = id by funext i; simp]
    76	    exact MvPolynomial.rename_id_apply g.1
    77	  · intro g
    78	    cases g with
    79	    | mk p hp =>
    80	        have hpoly : MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev
    81	            (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev p) = p := by
    82	          rw [MvPolynomial.rename_rename]
    83	          rw [show Fin.rev ∘ Fin.rev = id by funext i; simp]
    84	          exact MvPolynomial.rename_id_apply p
    85	        apply ldtPolynomial_ext
    86	        exact hpoly
    87	
    88	@[simp] theorem directPolyEquivPolynomial_poly
    89	    (D : DirectLdParams) (g : PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d) :
    90	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    91	    (directPolyEquivPolynomial D g).poly = MvPolynomial.rename Fin.rev g.1 := by
    92	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
    93	  rfl
    94	
    95	/-- The polynomial equivalence commutes with evaluation after the direct point
    96	and scalar codings. -/
    97	@[simp] theorem directPolyEquivPolynomial_apply
    98	    (D : DirectLdParams) (g : PolyIndex D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d)
    99	    (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) :
   100	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   101	    directPolyEquivPolynomial D g (directPointEquiv D u) =
   102	      directScalarEquiv D (MvPolynomial.eval u g.1) := by
   103	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   104	  unfold MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial.toFun evalPolynomialModel
   105	  rw [directPolyEquivPolynomial_poly]
   106	  unfold decodePoint
   107	  rw [MvPolynomial.eval_rename]
   108	  congr 1
   109	  apply congrArg (fun v : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D =>
   110	    MvPolynomial.eval v g.1)
   111	  funext i
   112	  simp only [Function.comp_apply, directPointEquiv_apply, Fin.rev_rev]
   113	  change (directScalarEquiv D).symm (directScalarEquiv D (u i)) = u i
   114	  exact (directScalarEquiv D).symm_apply_apply (u i)

   118	/-- Regard a complete LDT measurement as a matrix-valued QPBT
   119	measurement, with exactly the same effects. -/
   120	noncomputable def ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement
   121	    {alpha iota : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   122	    (M : MIPStarRE.LDT.Measurement alpha iota) :
   123	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota :=
   124	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne M.outcome M.outcome_pos (by
   125	    rw [M.sum_eq_total, M.total_eq_one])

   127	@[simp] theorem ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement_effect
   128	    {alpha iota : Type*} [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   129	    (M : MIPStarRE.LDT.Measurement alpha iota) (a : alpha) :
   130	    (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement M).effect a = M.outcome a :=
   131	  rfl

   133	/-- Relabel an LDT polynomial projective measurement by direct QPBT
   134	polynomial representatives. -/
   135	noncomputable def directPolynomialMeasurement
   136	    (D : DirectLdParams) :
   137	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   138	    {iota : Type*} → [Fintype iota] → [DecidableEq iota] →
   139	      ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) iota →
   140	        PolyMeas D.m (DirectScalarQ D) D.d iota := by
   141	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   142	  intro iota _ _ G
   143	  exact matrixMeasurementTransport (directPolyEquivPolynomial D).symm
   144	    (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement G.toMeasurement)

   146	@[simp] theorem directPolynomialMeasurement_effect

   153	        G.outcome (directPolyEquivPolynomial D g) := by

   155	  intro iota _ _ G g

   158	/-- Extract one polynomial coordinate from a direct polynomial-tuple POVM. -/

   201	/-- Evaluating the transported polynomial measurement is the relabeling of
   202	the LDT evaluation postprocessing through `directScalarEquiv`. -/
   203	theorem directPolynomialMeasurement_evaluation_effect
   204	    (D : DirectLdParams) :
   205	    letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   206	    ∀ {iota : Type*} [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   207	      (G : ProjMeas (MIPStarRE.LDT.Polynomial D.toLDTParameters) iota)
   208	      (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) (a : DirectScalarQ D),
   209	      ((directPolynomialMeasurement D G).postprocess
   210	        (fun g => MvPolynomial.eval u g.1)).effect a =
   211	        (ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement
   212	          (ProjMeas.postprocess G
   213	            (fun g => g (directPointEquiv D u))).toMeasurement).effect
   214	            (directScalarEquiv D a) := by
   215	  letI := D.toLDTFieldModel
   216	  intro iota _ _ G u a
   217	  classical
   218	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   219	  rw [ldtMeasurementToMatrixMeasurement_effect,
   220	    ProjMeas.postprocess, SubMeas.postprocess_outcome]
   221	  apply Finset.sum_bij (fun g _ => directPolyEquivPolynomial D g)
   222	  · intro g hg
   223	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hg ⊢
   224	    simpa only [directPolyEquivPolynomial_apply] using
   225	      congrArg (directScalarEquiv D) hg
   226	  · intro g₁ _ g₂ _ h
   227	    exact (directPolyEquivPolynomial D).injective h
   228	  · intro g hg
   229	    refine ⟨(directPolyEquivPolynomial D).symm g, ?_, ?_⟩
   230	    · simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hg ⊢
   231	      have heval := directPolyEquivPolynomial_apply D
   232	        ((directPolyEquivPolynomial D).symm g) u
   233	      rw [(directPolyEquivPolynomial D).apply_symm_apply] at heval
   234	      exact (directScalarEquiv D).injective (heval.symm.trans hg)
   235	    · exact (directPolyEquivPolynomial D).apply_symm_apply g
   236	  · intro g _
   237	    rw [directPolynomialMeasurement_effect]

   239	/-! ## Correlated-ancilla compression -/
   240	
   241	/-!
   242	The diagonal-block conditional expectation preserves either mixed defect
   243	exactly because the point measurement on the opposite carrier is constant on
   244	the residue register.  It does not yield a global/global compression theorem:
   245	the lifted state pairs equal residues, whereas separately compressing both
   246	polynomial measurements produces an independent double average over residues.
   247	Neither quantity bounds the other in general.  This open obstruction is
   248	recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
   249	-/
   250	
   251	/-- The normalized diagonal-block average of an operator on a carrier with a
   252	finite ancillary register.  This is the local conditional expectation used to
   253	discard one half of the correlated seed-residue ancilla. -/
   254	noncomputable def averageDiagonalBlock
   255	    {iota block : Type*} [Fintype iota] [Fintype block]
   256	    (A : Op (iota × block)) : Op iota := by
   257	  classical
   258	  exact (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   259	    ∑ r, A.submatrix (fun i => (i, r)) (fun i => (i, r))
   260	
   261	/-- Compress a POVM through the normalized diagonal-block average.  The
   262	nonemptiness assumption says precisely that the normalized finite average is
   263	defined over at least one ancillary basis element. -/
   264	noncomputable def correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement
   265	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   266	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   267	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   268	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block)) :
   269	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota :=
   270	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   271	    (fun a => averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a))
   272	    (fun a => by
   273	      unfold averageDiagonalBlock
   274	      apply smul_nonneg
   275	      · positivity
   276	      · exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun r _ =>
   277	          Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
   278	            ((Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (M.pos a)).submatrix
   279	              (fun i => (i, r))))
   280	    (by
   281	      classical
   282	      ext i j
   283	      simp only [averageDiagonalBlock, Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.smul_apply,
   284	        Matrix.submatrix_apply]
   285	      calc
   286	        ∑ a, (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   287	              ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) =
   288	            (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   289	              ∑ a, ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   290	                rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   291	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   292	              ∑ r, ∑ a, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by

210	\begin{definition}[Consistency between POVMs]\label{def:consistency}
   211		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.consistencyDefect, MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsConsistentWithin}
   212		\leanok
   213		\uses{def:povm-conventions, def:state-distance}
   214		Let $\mathcal X$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mathcal X$. Let $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal H_A \ot \mathcal H_B$ be a quantum state, and for all $x \in \mathcal X$ let $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ be POVMs. We write
   215		\[
   216			A^x_a \ot \Id_B \simeq_\delta \Id_A \ot B^x_a
   217		\]
   218		on state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ if
   219		\[
   220			\E_{x \sim \mu} \sum_{a \ne b} \bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^x_b \ket{\psi} = O(\delta)\,.
   221		\]
   222		In this case we say that $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ are \emph{$\delta$-consistent} on $\ket{\psi}$. As in Definition~\ref{def:state-distance}, the $O(\cdot)$ refers to families of POVMs and states indexed by an implicit parameter $n \in \N$, and is taken as $n \to \infty$.

   251	\subsubsection{Consistency between measurements}
   252	
   253	The most basic notion of similarity between two measurements is given by their \emph{consistency}.
   254	
   255	\begin{definition}[Consistency]\label{def:simeq}
   256	Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state in $\calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$.
   257	Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{A}}$
   258	and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on $\calH_{\mathrm{B}}$.
   259	Finally, let $\calD$ be a distribution on the question set~$\calX$.
   260	Then we say that
   261	 \begin{equation*}
   262	 A^x_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a
   263	 \end{equation*}
   264	  on state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\calD$ if
   265	  \begin{equation}\label{eq:no-big-Oh}
   266	  \E_{\bx \sim \calD} \sum_{a \neq b} \bra{\psi} A^{\bx}_a \ot B^{\bx}_b
   267	    \ket{\psi} \leq \delta.
   268	    \end{equation}
   269	\end{definition}
   270	
   271	This is simply the probability that the provers receive different outcomes
   272	when they measure with~$A$ and~$B$,
   273	assuming the sub-measurements do return an outcome.
   274	
   275	\begin{notation}[Simplifying notation]
   276	Because the state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\calD$ are typically clear from context,
   277	we will often write ``$ A^x_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a$"
   278	as shorthand for ``$ A^x_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a$ on state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\calD$".
   279	In the case when $\calD$ is not clear by context,
   280	we might specify it implicitly in terms of a random variable~$\bx$ distributed according to~$\calD$.
   281	For example, suppose the distribution~$\calD$ is supposed to be uniform on the question set $\F_q$.
   282	Then we might say ``on average over $\bx \sim \F_q$,
   283	\begin{equation*}
   284	A^x_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a"
   285	\end{equation*}
   286	as shorthand for ``$ A^x_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a$ on distribution $\calD$".
   287	\end{notation}
   288	
   289	We note that there are two differences between the definition of consistency in \Cref{def:simeq}
   290	and the original definition of consistency given in \cite[Definition 4.11]{NW19}.
   291	The first of these is that the~\cite{NW19} definition
   292	allows the right-hand side of \Cref{eq:no-big-Oh} to be $O(\delta)$
   293	rather than strictly~$\delta$.
   294	The benefit of this is that they do not need to keep track of constant prefactors in their proofs;
   295	we have elected to use this more concrete definition
   296	to make our proofs more easily verifiable, at the expense of tracking these constant prefactors.
   297	The second difference is that is that they define their consistency as the quantity
   298	\begin{equation*}
   299	1 - \E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{\bx}_a \ot B^{\bx}_a \ket{\psi}.
   300	\end{equation*}
   301	As we show below in \Cref{prop:simeq-for-measurements},
   302	this agrees with \Cref{def:simeq}
   303	when~$A$ and~$B$ are both measurements.
   304	However, these two definitions disagree
   305	when~$A$ and~$B$ are \emph{sub}-measurements,
   306	which is a case we will frequently encounter throughout this paper.
   307	
   308	\begin{proposition}[Consistency for measurements]\label{prop:simeq-for-measurements}
   309	Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ be two measurements.
   310	Then
   311	\begin{equation*}
   312	A^x_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot B^x_a
   313	\end{equation*}
   314	if and only if
   315	\begin{equation*}
   316	\E_{\bx} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{\bx}_a \ot B^{\bx}_a \ket{\psi} \geq 1 - \delta.
   317	\end{equation*}
   318	\end{proposition}
   319	\begin{proof}
   320	We compute
   321	\begin{align*}
   322	&\E_{\bx} \sum_{a \neq b}\bra{\psi} A^{\bx}_a \ot B^{\bx}_b \ket{\psi}\\
   323	=~& \E_{\bx} \sum_b \bra{\psi} \Big(\sum_{a \neq b} A^{\bx}_a\Big) \ot B^{\bx}_b\ket{\psi}\\
   324	=~&\E_{\bx} \sum_b \bra{\psi} (I - A^{\bx}_b) \ot B^{\bx}_b\ket{\psi}
   325		\tag{because~$A$ is a measurement}\\

+\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for the consistency conclusions in directly indexed coordinates]
+	\label{lem:direct-ld-consistency-coordinates}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPointPolynomial_consistencyDefect_le}
+	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.directPolynomialPoint_consistencyDefect_le}

+	This is not a named statement of \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. It records the
+	form in which the approximate-agreement conclusions of
+	Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} are available for the directly indexed
+	presentation of the classical low individual degree game, in which the
+	sampled coordinate is carried by the question itself rather than by a
+	residue class of $\F_q$; that presentation, and the divisibility
+	obstruction motivating it, are the subject of
+	Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility}.
+
+	Let $\delta \ge 0$, let $(\psi, A, B)$ be a projective strategy for the
+	directly indexed game, and let $G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$ be
+	measurements on $\hilb_{\mathrm A}$ and $\hilb_{\mathrm B}$ whose
+	outcomes are single polynomials of individual degree at most $d$ in $m$
+	variables. Fix one coordinate $r \in \{1, \dots, k\}$ of the answer
+	tuple and write $A^{\mathsf{Point},\,u,\,r}$ and
+	$B^{\mathsf{Point},\,u,\,r}$ for the point measurements of the two
+	players read out at that coordinate. Then:
+	\begin{enumerate}
+		\item if, over a uniformly random point $u \in \F_q^m$,
+		      $A^{\mathsf{Point},\,u,\,r} \ot I_{\mathrm B}$ and
+		      $I_{\mathrm A} \ot G^{\mathrm B}_{[g(u) = a]}$ satisfy the
+		      relation $\simeq_{\delta}$ of
+		      Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness} on the density operator of
+		      $\psi$, then the off-diagonal defect of
+		      Definition~\ref{def:consistency} of that same pair, written
+		      in the directly indexed question and answer types and
+		      evaluated on the vector $\psi$, is at most $\delta$;
+		\item the same statement with the two players exchanged, for
+		      $G^{\mathrm A}_{[g(u) = a]} \ot I_{\mathrm B}$ and
+		      $I_{\mathrm A} \ot B^{\mathsf{Point},\,u,\,r}$;
+		\item if $G^{\mathrm A} \ot I_{\mathrm B}$ and
+		      $I_{\mathrm A} \ot G^{\mathrm B}$ satisfy that relation,
+		      taken over the one-element question set, then the
+		      off-diagonal defect of the corresponding pair in the
+		      directly indexed answer type is at most $\delta$.
+	\end{enumerate}

+	only for that coordinate, and all three take single polynomials rather
+	than tuples as the outcomes of $G^{\mathrm A}$ and $G^{\mathrm B}$.
+	None of them constructs the joint measurement of a whole $k$-tuple of
+	polynomials asserted by Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}; that
+	construction is not established here.

+	Let $(\psi, A, B)$ be a strategy for the classical game with parameters
+	$(q,m,d,k)$, and extend it to the directly indexed game by adjoining to
+	each player a register of dimension $q/m$, the common size of the

   293	## 10. `agent.sh` versus `autofix.sh`
   294	
   295	`docs/pr_review_management.md` keeps a behavioural matrix for the `@claude` and
   296	`@codex` responders — mentions fire only from comments and never from bodies;
   297	`@codex` on an issue always forks a fresh PR from `main`, causing PR
   298	proliferation; `@claude` on a PR pushes to the branch but failed outright on
   299	branch names containing `]`, root-caused to `claude-code-action`'s branch-name
   300	validation and fixed by adopting bracket-free naming
   301	(`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).

   303	The local translation is:

   305	| Parent | Local | Who starts it |
   306	|---|---|---|
   307	| `@claude` on a PR comment | `local/bin/agent.sh <pr-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
   308	| `@codex` on an issue | `local/bin/agent.sh <issue-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |

390	## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)
   391	
   392	A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
   393	the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:
   394	
   395	1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   396	   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   397	   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   398	   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   399	   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   400	   `moot: <reason>`);
   401	2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
   402	3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
   403	4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   404	   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.
   405	
   406	Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
   407	This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
   408	terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.
   409	
   410	## 13. Evidence follows the diff: carry-forward across a fresh-base (2026-09-04)
   411	
   412	The merge gate's fresh-base rule (issues-prs.md, gate 2b) moves a PR's head
   413	every time `main` advances, but a merge of `main` into the branch does not
   414	change the PR's own patch.  `review.sh` therefore compares a whitespace-
   415	sensitive hash of the patch (the diff without its `index`/hunk-header lines,
   416	so hunk positions may move but no byte of content may) with that of every
   417	earlier reviewed head of the same PR whose review is bound to that head and
   418	published by the lane's account; on a match it republishes that head's verdict

# Mathematical Language Guidelines

MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
the formalization with the paper and blueprint.

This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.

## Scope

These guidelines apply to:

- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
- module docstrings;
- declaration docstrings;
- documentation-visible section comments;
- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
- issue titles and issue bodies;
- PR titles and PR descriptions.

## Source of Truth

Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:

1. `references/ldt-paper/`
2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files

When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.

## Reference Notation And Terminology

The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.

When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
first applicable location in the following order:

1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
   differs from the paper;
2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
   family of declarations in that file;
3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
   blueprint;
4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.

The explanation should say:

- the notation or term used in the paper;
- the Lean object or name which represents it;
- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
- the scope in which the replacement should be used.

A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
where future readers can learn it.

Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.

## Naming Norm

Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled.

Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
clearer phrase.

This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
number, or implementation history.

### Concrete examples

The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
paper or blueprint would recognize.

| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |

An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.

File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.

### Shared helpers

When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.

Procedure:

1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   explicit argument.
2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   blueprint location it supports.

### Legacy identifier treatment

If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.

Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.

## Review Checklist

Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.

- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
      implementation-phase labels)?
- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
      source does not use them that way?
- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
      that order of preference?
- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
      construction they support?
- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.

Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
relevant audit before changing names or prose.

     6	/-!
     7	# The low-degree game
     8	
     9	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    10	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    11	the ambient coefficient space; their conditional-linearity and distribution
    12	invariants are recorded as proof-level obligations for later stages.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    17	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`; their paper origin is
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    31	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    32	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    33	`def:ld-game` in
    34	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    36	-/
    37	structure LdParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  k : ℕ
    42	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    43	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    44	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    45	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    46	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    47	
    48	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    49	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    50	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    51	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    52	
    53	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    54	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
    55	parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    57	-/
    58	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    59	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    60	
    61	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    62	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    63	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    64	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    65	-/
    66	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    67	
    68	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    69	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    70	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    71	-/
    72	inductive LdType where
    73	  | point
    74	  | aline
    75	  | dline
    76	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    77	
    78	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    79	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    80	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    81	-/
    82	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    83	
    84	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    85	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    87	-/
    88	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    89	
    90	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    91	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    92	-/
    93	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    94	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    95	
    96	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    97	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    98	-/
    99	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
   100	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
   101	
   102	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   103	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   104	-/
   105	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   106	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   107	
   108	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   109	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   110	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   112	-/
   113	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   114	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   115	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   116	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   117	
   118	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   119	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   120	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   121	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   122	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   123	-/
   124	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   125	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   126	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   127	
   128	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   129	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   130	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   132	-/
   133	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   134	  fun i => match i with
   135	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   136	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   137	  | .inr _ => 0
   138	
   139	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   140	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   141	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   142	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   143	-/
   144	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   145	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   146	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   147	  fun i => match i with
   148	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   149	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   150	  | .inr _ => 0
   151	
   152	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   153	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   154	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   155	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   156	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   157	-/
   158	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   159	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   160	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   161	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   162	  fun i => match i with
   163	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   164	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   165	  | .inr j => direction j
   166	
   167	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   168	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   169	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin

   279	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=

   282	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   283	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   284	  | _, _ => false

   290	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   291	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   292	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   293	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   294	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   295	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   296	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →

   299	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin

   303	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   304	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   305	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   306	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   307	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   308	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j

   310	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   311	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   312	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   313	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   314	-/
   315	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   316	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   317	  open Classical in
   318	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   319	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   320	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   321	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   322	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   323	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   324	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   325	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   327	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   328	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   329	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   330	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   331	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   332	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   333	      else false
   334

   336	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin

   338	-/

   340	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   341	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   342	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   343	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   344	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   345	  μ_prob := (uniformDistribution_isProbability
   346	    ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)).map _
   347	  decide := ldWinPredicate P

   349	end

Coarse-graining therefore only merges terms of the off-diagonal sum, so the post-processed off-diagonal mass is at most the original one.

  1892		\label{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility}
  1893		Definition~\ref{def:ld-game} defines the classical low individual
  1894		degree game only when its dimension parameter divides $q$: the index
  1895		function $\chi$ of the question distribution
  1896		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}) partitions $\F_q$ into
  1897		classes of equal size, one for each coordinate. The same divisibility
  1898		underlies the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$
  1899		(Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist} instantiated at dimension
  1900		$2m+2$), and with it the statements of Lemmas~\ref{lem:qld-sublines}
  1901		and~\ref{lem:qld-4-13} and the proofs of all three of
  1902		Lemmas~\ref{lem:qld-sublines}, \ref{lem:qld-4-13}
  1903		and~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}. The condition that $2m+2$ divide $q$ does not
  1904		follow from admissibility of $(q,m,d)$
  1905		(Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), which supplies only that $m$
  1906		divides $q$; indeed the two are jointly satisfiable only in a
  1907		degenerate range. An admissible field size
  1908		(Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}) is a power of two, so $m$
  1909		dividing $q$ forces $m$ to be a power of two; for $m \ge 2$ the
  1910		integer $m+1$ is odd and exceeds $1$, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ divides no
  1911		power of two, while for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for
  1912		every admissible $q$ except $q = 2$. The source proof in

  1917		blocked at the marked steps, so the conclusions are not established

  1921		applies to dimensions not dividing $q$; the missing step and the
